description: Solo participant building an AI-powered autonomous path-planning and hazard-avoidance navigation system for Martian rovers using NASA's geospatial and surface data. Focused on robust space robotics and secure mission telemetry.
summary: ARES-NAV 2.0 is a physics-informed 3D Geomorphic Digital Twin and Mission Operating System engineered to guide future crewed exploration across Mars' Jezero Crater. Static 2D maps fail to protect astronauts from extreme crater slopes (>22 degrees), regolith sinkage, dust storms, radiation, and strict Portable Life Support System (PLSS) oxygen limits. Our web application solves this by fusing NASA MOLA and HiRISE elevation models, Perseverance MEDA weather telemetry, and MRO SHARAD/CRISM subsurface prospecting data into an autonomous mission control engine. Key capabilities include a 3-corridor Pareto A* pathfinding solver balancing metabolic burn against oxygen reserves, an xEMU Visor AR HUD with real-time terrain ray-casting, subsurface water-ice detection for In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU), and a 30-model planetary physics suite verified with 100% Pytest accuracy.
details:
ARES-NAV 2.0 is an advanced Autonomous Martian EVA & ISRU Digital Twin OS engineered for Jezero Crater exploration.

What it does & How it works:

The system fuses high-resolution NASA MOLA and HiRISE DEM geospatial raster layers with live Perseverance MEDA weather telemetry and MRO SHARAD/CRISM subsurface radar data. It features a 3-corridor Pareto A* pathfinding solver that balances metabolic burn, oxygen consumption, and terrain slopes against rover kinematics.

Tools, Tech Stack & Hardware:

- Frontend & Geospatial Engine: Python, Streamlit, Plotly, PyDeck.

- Physics & Algorithms: NumPy, SciPy, custom Pytest verification suite (30 mathematical solvers).

- Data Sources: NASA Planetary Data System (PDS), MOLA, HiRISE, MEDA, SHARAD, CRISM.

🌐 Open-Source GitHub Repository & Code:

https://github.com/azizaalampushpo/ares-nav-mars-os

Team ShunnyaVerse has verified 100% of the planetary physics models to ensure mission safety and prevent rover rollover or astronaut PLSS exhaustion.
